commit_attribution: Primary human-authorized operator session performed all inspection, tooling, experimentation, and finalization/commit/push directly. DELEGATED .3 FINALIZATION / COMMIT / PUSH: UNAUTHORIZED preserved (no delegated worker used in this phase).
summary: Redesigned the predecessor's non-resumable continuous single-process execution-time trace (RESUME MODEL C: ~80/571 files in one process, ~140-minute full-suite projection, explicitly not validly resumable at file 81 in a fresh process) into RESUME MODEL A: 31 independent 25-file batch-vs-victim compositions over a frozen 761-file corpus (corpus grew since the predecessor's ~571 figure), each unit run from a fresh clean process and checkpointed immediately after. Built and independently verified a durable checkpoint mechanism (schema, chain-linking via previous_checkpoint_digest, atomic temp-file-then-replace persistence, self_digest tamper-detection) before any coverage invocation: restart-readability, corruption-refusal, corpus-drift-refusal, and tracer-drift-refusal were each tested against disposable tampered copies and all passed -- CHECKPOINT METHOD: VERIFIED. Verified the diagnostic tracer (id()/module/qualname watch on HPACStoreAuthority and HumanPrincipalRegistryStore) was non-interfering via a victim-alone with/without-tracer control (identical outcome both times). Did not import any of the predecessor's three ad hoc clusters (15 CLTR-authority files, 22 multiprocessing files, an unreconstructable 55-file thematic cluster) as checkpointed coverage, since their exact membership could not be independently re-verified against the new batch boundaries with confidence -- inherited coverage: 0/31, per this phase's own instruction to leave unsupportable units PENDING rather than guess. Ran 26 batch invocations (~49.0 min) plus 2 tracer-validation controls (~7s) plus one aborted 600s-timeout attempt at batch-000 before the driver's timeout handling was hardened (crashed without writing a checkpoint entry, its wall-clock time still counted): 29 of 30 authorized invocations, ~59.2 of 60 authorized minutes -- both budgets effectively exhausted (Stop Condition B). Results: 18/31 batches CLEAN (no victim failure, id() stable start-to-finish); 7/31 INCONCLUSIVE (hit the 240s per-invocation timeout, batches 0/4/7/11/12/17/25); 5/31 not yet attempted; and 1/31 -- batch-013 (25 files spanning the 146g/146h1/146h3/146l/147g-q/148c7-g2/149d/149g/149j/149m/149n/149o_10* clusters) -- shows a new high-confidence lead: id(HPACStoreAuthority) and id(HumanPrincipalRegistryStore) both changed between session-start and session-finish (module/qualname strings unchanged -- the signature of a class object being replaced by a same-named-but-distinct object), correlated with the victim module's first-ever non-clean outcome anywhere in this diagnostic lineage (2 ERRORs: test_94_counter_missing_fails_closed_not_zero, test_95_assurance_class_of_enrolled_records_is_production). Re-checking all 18 other completed batches' trace pairs confirms id() stability in every one of them -- batch-013 is unique among 19 batches with complete trace pairs. This is a strong evidence-motivated correlation, NOT a causal proof: no post-finding victim-alone re-control, no within-batch bisection of the 25 files, no trigger-removal control, and no fresh-process repeat were performed (budget was exhausted producing/discovering the finding itself, which cost zero additional invocations beyond the 26-invocation sweep that generated the trace files). VERDICT: CONTAMINATION ROOT CAUSE: UNRESOLVED. CONTAMINATION STAGE: TEST-EXECUTION (unchanged). CONTAMINATION LOCATION: NOT ESTABLISHED. CURRENT F-5 READINESS: NOT YET ESTABLISHED. F-5 EXECUTION HOLD: REMAINS. N-16-5 remains NOT CLOSED; N-16-6/N-16-7 untouched. No production/existing-test/contract/dependency modification; no host mutation; no F-5 action; no YubiKey/human ceremony; no historical Telegram re-dispatch.
